## Independent adversarial review — Shared Calendar/Notes

Baseline `b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f`; live issue, Notes guide/README, store, CRUD/action and earlier plan read. No hosted CRUD or storage migration executed.

### P1 — Content deduplication is not a cross-tier migration identity

[Notes create](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/plugins/plugin-notes/src/service.ts#L283) defines replay by noteContentKey rather than operation identity. [Update](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/plugins/plugin-notes/src/service.ts#L339) removes other records matching either the previous or resulting content key and returns consolidated IDs. The existing single-agent store intentionally owns this behavior. A Shared migration which merges eligible free notes with Dedicated-derived notes, then reuses that content key, can collapse records with distinct provenance/retention authority. Identical text is not proof of identical authority or original identity.

Amendment: define ownership/provenance filtering before lookup, deduplication, mutation and rendering; never let a common content key cross that boundary. Preserve original record IDs plus migration identity mapping/tombstones; do not flatten protected Dedicated history into the eligible Free namespace. Make same-content semantics explicit within one authorized collection. Acceptance: identical content in eligible and ineligible stores; only eligible rows participate in Shared read/update/delete and cutover, protected rows stay unchanged, and restart/fallback does not resurrect or merge them. This is an unsafe-migration counterexample to prevent, not a demonstrated deployed cross-tier exposure. Detailed authorization remains server derived.

### P2 — Replayed create is currently a new revision but its effect receipt says fresh

The store [transact](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/plugins/plugin-notes/src/store.ts#L202) always increments revision and writes, including createNoteWithCommit's content-replay branch. That branch suppresses the state-updated event. The action then exposes replayed in data, but [committed receipt](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/plugins/plugin-notes/src/action.ts#L87) hardcodes idempotency.key=null/replayed=false and uses a new timestamp receipt ID. Thus a replay can change clear-confirmation revision without notification and report inconsistent replay semantics to the planner/evidence system. These are source-proven current contracts; the intended content-idempotent behavior is already explicit in service code.

Amendment: introduce durable request-key replay in the canonical operation result and return the original committed revision/receipt for exact replay. Define no-op content dedup distinctly from request replay. Store transactions need an explicit unchanged outcome if no revision should advance; any revision that does advance must be reflected consistently to clients. Feed the real operation result into effect receipts instead of regenerating fresh identity. Test duplicate requests before/after restart, concurrent create with same/different content, clear confirmation followed only by replay, and actual emitted snapshot/receipt parity. Retain the existing clear expectedRevision check inside the storage transaction; do not move it into an API precheck.

### P2 — Update and deletion compatibility must survive storage extraction

Current Notes update uses whole-content replacement and consolidation, not a field-merge/CAS patch contract. The previous plan's generic "conflict/version checks" needs a declared API migration: adding expectedRevision must not silently break existing view/action callers, and retaining unconditional last-writer-wins must not be advertised as conflict-safe. Introduce explicit versioned operation inputs or an adapter preserving old semantics; migrate UI and action callers together. Test concurrent view edit and chat edit against real persistent Shared storage, ambiguous lookup after another writer changes content, delete/retry, and lost response recovery.

This review does not duplicate the earlier Calendar provider/recurrence plan. Calendar source is still a separate domain owner; Notes extraction must not borrow its schema or scheduler. Existing OWNER gating protects the per-agent local store; a Shared port needs the server-resolved account identity because runtime/agent membership alone is not a storage tenancy contract.

topPRs.body:
# Relates to

Closes #30598. Adds the Eliza Cloud boundary required by Outreachr's hosted CRM.

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] Targets `develop`; rebased onto `7bb7938d1e397` without conflicts.
- [x] Post-sync `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passed; `bun run verify` passed.
- [x] Reproducible behavior and validation limits are recorded below.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Rebased onto the latest fetched `origin/develop`; zero conflicts.
- [x] Final post-sync verification passed at `8384d56f5c41d45f91eae3c1f08d79c96e981be7`.

# Risks

Medium: introduces a credential-bearing API boundary and a separate product's Stripe operations. Routes require a registered app and hashed client secret. User delegation is short-lived, revocable, and checked against primary account authority; Google ownership remains enforced by the managed connector service. Billing validates app/workspace/customer/price metadata and verifies Stripe webhook signatures. All new routes remain unavailable until explicit Outreachr bindings are configured.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Outreachr can exchange its existing app-login code for scoped identity and managed Google access without copying Google credentials into the CRM. The primary database retains an authorization-code digest so replay stays blocked even after grant revocation or a stale cache read. Google transport permits only the Gmail/calendar operations used by the CRM.

The billing boundary reuses Cloud's Stripe service for separate Outreachr workspace customers and monthly seat prices. Stable idempotency keys protect customer and checkout creation; current subscriptions are read from Stripe and webhooks are signature-verified. Existing Cloud products and subscriptions are not changed.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature; additive backend routes and an append-only delegation migration.

# Documentation changes needed?

Deployment bindings and migration order are documented in the companion Outreachr cloud README and implementation plan. Apply `0376_outreachr_delegations.sql` before enabling the routes; configure the exact app ID/origin/client-secret digest plus Sol/Astra price IDs and a dedicated webhook secret. Use the standard staging certification and production approval workflow.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`outreachr-delegation.test.ts`, `outreachr-billing.test.ts`, and `outreachr-delegations-migration.pglite.test.ts` under `packages/cloud/shared/src`.
